But more importantly, the issue is that the postcondition should just be `max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[i]` for all valid i, j.

But `i` here is a bound variable in the forall. So for `i = 0`, the postcondition requires `max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[0] && 0 != 0`, which simplifies to `max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[0] && false`, which is `false`.

Wait no. If `i = 0`, then `i != 0` is `false`, so the entire conjunction is `false`. So the postcondition requires that for all `i, j` with `0 <= i < j < prices.Length`, we have `max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[i] && i != 0`. When `i = 0`, this becomes `false`. So the postcondition is actually unsatisfiable (it requires `false` to be true for `i = 0` cases).

Wait, that can't be right. Let me re-read the quantifier. `forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < prices.Length ==> max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[i] && i != 0`.

So for ALL i, j where 0 <= i < j < prices.Length, we need: (max_profit >= prices[j] - prices[i]) AND (i != 0).

When i = 0, i != 0 is false, so the whole thing is false. But the postcondition must hold for ALL i, j in range. So when i = 0 and j = 1 (assuming length >= 2), the postcondition requires false. This means the postcondition is UNSATISFIABLE for any array of length >= 2.

So the postcondition is wrong. The intended postcondition should be:
```

```

The `&& i != 0` was accidentally included and makes the postcondition impossible to satisfy.
